description: Upgrade the sandbox base from Debian Bookworm to Debian Trixie while preserving toolchain, ownership, and optional installer contracts.

userStories.title: Move the Dockerfile to Trixie
userStories.description: As a sandbox operator, I want the image to track Debian stable so its distribution packages and support runway remain current.
acceptanceCriteria: .devcontainer/Dockerfile uses FROM debian:trixie-slim
Docker's apt repository uses trixie while Cloudflare's remains bookworm with an adjacent HTTP 404 explanation
A focused deterministic test guards the base and repository suite decisions
CHANGELOG.md has one imperative issue-linked entry under Unreleased Changed within 250 characters
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: 2026-08-26: Dockerfile on debian:trixie-slim, Docker apt suite trixie, Cloudflare pinned bookworm with 404 comment; guarded by sandbox-base-image.test.ts (commit 3af58a1c).

userStories.title: Reconcile runtime and documentation claims
userStories.description: As a sandbox user, I want runtime diagnostics and documentation to describe Trixie and the remaining KVM requirement accurately.
acceptanceCriteria: Runtime source keeps the glibc 2.39 and /dev/kvm prerequisites without claiming the current image fails glibc
Runtime tests and runtime-preflight-gate.sh guard current semantics while retaining intentional historical parser fixtures
Installation, runtime RFC, DebugMCP, and MicroSandbox docs describe Trixie and only /dev/kvm as the current default blocker
No runtime selector, device passthrough, configuration key, or MicroSandbox installation is added
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: 2026-08-26: catalog glibc remediation now names debian:trixie-slim, /dev/kvm kept as the sole remaining blocker; docs + runtime-preflight-gate.sh reconciled, historical 2.35/2.36 parser fixtures retained (commit b70cd319).

userStories.title: Verify the default image and ownership contract
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want reusable image and boot verification so a base upgrade cannot silently remove tools or change ownership behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: A documented image verifier checks Trixie, apt suites, UID/GID 1000, Node 22, pnpm 10.33.0, required tools, Herdr 0.7.4, and architecture-specific Herdr checksum
sandbox-boot-smoke.sh verifies runtime UID/GID and sandbox-created bind-file ownership against the checkout owner
The existing Validate sandbox compose and image build job keeps its name, runs the verifier, and completes compose boot smoke
PR evidence compares exact node and pnpm versions between unchanged Bookworm base and Trixie candidate
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: 2026-08-26: verify-sandbox-image.sh (13 tests) + boot-smoke bind-ownership checks (5 tests) + boot-guard job wiring, job name unchanged; node/pnpm parity mechanism shipped as node-pnpm-parity.sh and a dispatch-only workflow, the evidence run itself requires a Docker daemon and executes in CI (commit 3866a69d).

userStories.title: Validate arm64 and optional installers
userStories.description: As a release maintainer, I want Dockerfile-scoped compatibility CI so both architectures and all optional installers are exercised before release.
acceptanceCriteria: A Dockerfile-path-scoped workflow builds and verifies a default arm64 image
One amd64 image builds with INSTALL_HERMES, INSTALL_DEEPAGENTS, INSTALL_OPENCODE, and INSTALL_GROK_BUILD true and all four binaries report versions
The workflow uses read-only repository permissions and performs no registry login or push
sandbox-boot-guard-ci.sh guards architecture, optional build, verifier, and no-push contracts without adding a probe
.github/workflows/release.yml remains unchanged
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: 2026-08-26: sandbox-compatibility.yml builds/verifies arm64 (native runner or QEMU) and one all-optional amd64 image reporting four CLI versions, read-only and push-free; sandbox-boot-guard-ci.sh extended in place, release.yml untouched (commit 953f7dc4).
